key_insight: The paper shows that adding LCNot-UCCSD initialization and RBM-based configuration recovery can make quantum-selected CI workflows more efficient for molecular simulation on near-term and hybrid quantum platforms.
engineering_relevance: These ideas reduce classical preprocessing cost and improve subspace selection efficiency, making quantum-assisted electronic-structure methods more practical for drug-discovery and protein-ligand studies.
method: LCNot-UCCSD replaces costly CCSD initialization with MP2-amplitude initialization inside QSCI.
QSCI-RBM uses a Restricted Boltzmann Machine to recover and expand configuration subspaces.
The workflow is tested within DMET for larger chemically relevant systems, including Amantadine and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease complexed with Carmofur.
evidence_signal: Evaluation includes eight molecules in STO-3G across 14 artificial error levels with 100 runs each, plus N2 potential energy surface scans in cc-pVDZ and DMET case studies on Amantadine and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease complex.
watch_item: Results are based on an ideal state-vector simulator and controlled error studies, so real hardware noise, scaling overheads, and RBM training stability may affect performance in practice.
paper_title: Bridging the NISQ and Fault-Tolerant Regimes: Generative-ML-Assisted Quantum Selected CI for Molecular Simulations
